signals.title: NZD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Policy Divergence
signals.text: The G10 Currency Strength Scorecard registers a 3.721% leader-to-laggard spread over the one-week trailing window, establishing a critical bilateral divergence. JPY ranks first across the G10 with an average advance of +2.306% across seven pairs, while NZD trails at -1.416% across four pairs. Hawkish BoJ policy rhetoric contrasts with the RBNZ OCR at 2.75% and overnight cash at 2.7500%, alongside CFTC positioning where JPY leveraged funds net short sits at -111,297 contracts (pctl 2, z -2.18) and NZD net short stands at -23,004 contracts (pctl 4, z -1.81). NZD/USD technical structure shows the currency trading at 0.5884, slipping below its SMA20 at 0.5910 while remaining above the SMA50 and SMA200 cluster at 0.5839/0.5855. Implication: broad yen outperformance drives systematic unwinds across cross pairs despite an underlying carry deficit against high-beta counterparts. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/JPY, driven by broad JPY outperformance and multi-pair divergence. Catalyst: ECB meeting 10 Sep followed by BoJ meeting 18 Sep. Risk: JPY safe-haven and hawkish momentum reverses if US yields surge post-CPI, lifting cross carry pairs.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Downside Skew + Middle East Geopolitical Friction
signals.text: Spot USD/JPY trades at 156.23, holding below its SMA20 (158.96), SMA50 (160.48), and SMA200 (158.45). Geopolitical headlines citing Iranian restricted zone declarations near the Strait of Hormuz coincide with aggressive options positioning, where the 25d risk reversal prints at -2.54, indicating pronounced put skew. Implied volatility trades at 7.2% against 30-day realized volatility of 10.7%, generating a negative volatility risk premium of -3.5 points that highlights suppressed option pricing relative to recent daily swings. CFTC leveraged funds carry an extreme net short in JPY of -111,297 contracts (pctl 2, z -2.18) following a WoW expansion of -29,678 contracts, leaving long USD/JPY exposure vulnerable to rapid de-risking despite a 268bp SOFR-TONA carry advantage. Implication: elevated options hedging reflects positioning liquidation risk into geopolitical headlines rather than conventional safe-haven channel activation given contained equity volatility. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY, pressured by asymmetric downside options demand and crowded short positioning. Catalyst: US CPI release followed by FOMC meeting 16 Sep. Risk: Spot USD/JPY reclaims the SMA200 at 158.45, invalidating immediate downside continuation.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Positioning + Options + Retail Contrarian Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7208, maintaining position above its SMA20 (0.7135), SMA50 (0.7041), and SMA200 (0.6988). CFTC leveraged funds hold a crowded net long of +50,250 contracts, positioned in the 94th percentile of its 52-week historical range (z +1.79) despite a WoW reduction of -3,328 contracts. In contrast, retail positioning via Myfxbook displays an extreme 90% short stance (10% long), generating an institutional versus retail divergence. The OIS spread favors the Australian dollar with AONIA at 4.35% versus SOFR at 3.66% (-69bp carry premium for AUD), supported by RBA policy at 4.35% against the Fed at 3.75%. Implication: severe retail net short exposure risks a forced short squeeze higher, though stalling institutional leveraged flow warrants upside caution at current levels. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/USD, supported by positive carry and retail squeeze dynamics. Catalyst: US CPI release followed by RBA meeting 29 Sep. Risk: Spot closes below the SMA20 at 0.7135, signaling speculative exhaustion and unwinding of leveraged longs.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Volatility Premium + Neutral Policy Spread
signals.text: Cable trades at 1.3516, positioned below its SMA20 of 1.3555 but sustaining levels above the SMA50 at 1.3456 and SMA200 at 1.3447. The options complex shows elevated forward demand, with ATM implied volatility trading at 11.0% against realized 30-day volatility of 4.7%, printing an outsized volatility risk premium of +6.3 points. The monetary policy stance remains balanced with the Fed at 3.75% and the BoE at 3.75% yielding a 0bp nominal policy spread, mirrored in overnight rates where SONIA at 3.73% trades 7bp above SOFR at 3.66%. Leveraged funds retain a net long GBP position of +47,504 contracts at the 93rd percentile (z +1.27), though WoW reduction of -9,335 contracts indicates institutional profit taking. Implication: elevated option pricing indicates acute hedging ahead of major central bank cycles while spot consolidates within its daily moving average envelope. Trade bias: Neutral/range GBP/USD, constrained by balanced policy spreads and expensive protective options. Catalyst: BoE policy meeting 17 Sep. Risk: A decisive daily close below the SMA50/SMA200 support confluence at 1.3447/1.3456.
